title: AI scams in Georgia and South Florida: How scammers use deepfakes to steal millions

reading.body:
Scammers deployed AI tools to impersonate real people and organizations, targeting immigrants and others through deepfakes and voice cloning. An immigration attorney discovered criminals had cloned his voice to solicit payment for fake legal services. The systems were used outside any legitimate context, as tools built for other purposes were repurposed to commit fraud at scale.

The failure was not in the AI systems themselves but in their accessibility to bad actors and the absence of verification mechanisms on the receiving end. Victims lost significant sums because they had no reliable way to confirm they were communicating with legitimate attorneys or family members. Better outcomes would have required either restricting access to deepfake and voice-cloning tools, or establishing and using independent verification methods before transferring money or information.

It is not established how the AI tools were obtained, by what means they were deployed, or what specific companies provided them.

summary:
Scammers are increasingly using artificial intelligence technology to commit fraud across Georgia and South Florida. They employ deepfakes and voice cloning to impersonate trusted individuals, targeting victims through romance schemes, fake investment opportunities, and emergency calls. One South Florida immigration attorney discovered criminals had cloned his voice to target immigrants, while a Cobb County couple lost approximately $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam. According to the FBI's 2025 Internet Crime Report, Americans reported nearly $893 million in AI-enabled scam losses last year out of over $20 billion in total internet crime losses. Florida reported 350 AI-related complaints with $39.9 million in losses, while Georgia reported 71 complaints with $10.4 million in losses.

The technology allows criminals to make traditional scams more convincing by cloning voices from social media, spoofing phone numbers, creating fake photographs, and researching personal relationships. Romance and confidence scams resulted in over $19 million in losses nationwide, with voice-cloning distress scams accounting for more than $5 million. Experts recommend families establish code words to verify identities, verify urgent requests through known phone numbers, and avoid sending money based on phone calls alone. As AI tools become cheaper and more accessible, investigators warn the problem will likely worsen, making verification a critical defense against these scams.
